newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Star Mining sees progress on Russian Sukh.
newsitem.headline: Star Mining sees progress on Russian Sukh.

text.p: Russia has taken another step towards opening its giant Sukhoi Log gold field to foreign investors with a recent government decree which may ensure that a company set up to tap the field survives.

The document, signed by Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin and dated May 30, orders Lenzoloto, the Russian joint stock company in which Australian miner Star Mining Corp NL has a stake, to proceed to approve new charter documents and continue its activities.
Russia's Supreme Court had declared the privatisation of Lenzoloto, which has a licence to tap Sukhoi Log, illegal and asked for the company to be dissolved.
Star Mining's Graeme Ellis said Chernomyrdin had signed the document but that hurdles remained.
"With a project of this size, you're talking about half a billion dollars," he said, adding, "you have to establish the bankability of the project.
"We're looking at mineable reserves of approximately 40 million ounces."

Star holds a nearly 35 percent nominal stake in Lenzoloto though its unit Star Technology Systems Ltd. It will have 49 percent once Lenzoloto restructures after a June 28 general shareholders' meeting.
